conventions.convention: The state set and every statewise action set are finite and nonempty. Rewards lie in [0,1] with their Borel sigma-algebra. A joint next-state/reward kernel permits dependence between a reward and its accompanying next state. AC is assumed for policy path laws.

Hitting times start at time zero and equal +∞ if the target is never hit. Infima range over measurable history-dependent randomized policies. The normalized diameter is D=max{1,D₀}; a singleton has D₀=0 and D=1.
EVI uses a strict residual-span stopping test, fixed tie orders, and returns the vector u_(i−1) used in the terminating backup. Without a termination hypothesis the procedure is partial.

Interactions start at t=1. Episode-start counts exclude the current episode and remain frozen for its stopping threshold; an episode ends immediately after a pair reaches max{1,N_k(s,a)} within-episode visits.

ρ* is the common limit of optimal finite-horizon expected reward divided by horizon. Pathwise regret is the random variable Δ_T=Tρ*−R_T; expected regret is its expectation and pathwise regret can be negative.
The upper bounds are for each fixed horizon and initial state. The logarithm log(T/δ) requires integer T≥2; log(2T/δ) supplies the all-horizon version for integer T≥1.
The lower-bound environment is chosen after the learning algorithm and prescribed initial label. Its diameter is at most D, with D≥max{1,20 log_A S}; the guarantee concerns expected regret.

load_bearing.statement: A finite nonempty state set and finite nonempty statewise action sets carry a probability kernel Q from admissible state-action pairs to S×[0,1]. Conditional on observed history and the selected action, the next-state/reward pair has this law. AC is assumed for policy path laws.
The MDP is communicating if inf_π E_x^π[τ_y]<∞ for every ordered pair (x,y). Its raw diameter is D₀=sup_(x,y) inf_π E_x^π[τ_y], and its normalized diameter is D=max{1,D₀}.

For finite nonempty state/action systems, probability-vector centers and finite nonnegative transition radii, the transfer routine returns an exact feasible row maximizer using at most 2|S|+1 positive transfers. With finite upper rewards, positive tolerance and strictly positive radii, EVI terminates and its returned quantities are measurable under fixed tie orders. With η=min_(s,a) min{1,b_p(s,a)/2}>0, span(u_i−u_(i−1))≤(1−η)^(i−1) span(u₁), with zero span for i≥2 when η=1.

Assume AC for path-law and conditional-expectation constructions. For a finite communicating MDP with rewards in [0,1], let V_n(s) be the supremum of expected first-n reward sums over history-dependent policies from s. The limit V_n(s)/n exists for every s, is independent of s, and belongs to [0,1].

Under AC, a finite-horizon interaction with a measurable nonanticipating policy whose randomization is independent of unexposed MDP samples admits an enlarged-space representation with the same observed interaction law: each pair's jth observation is the jth coordinate of a fixed independent sample sequence with law Q(·|s,a), whenever that visit occurs.

Under AC, for a length-T nonanticipating interaction in a bounded-reward finite MDP with S≥1 states and at most A≥1 actions per state, integer T≥1 and δ∈(0,1), with probability at least 1−δ all observed pair prefixes simultaneously satisfy |r̂_n−r|≤sqrt(7 log(4SAT/δ)/(2n)) and ‖P̂_n−P‖₁≤sqrt(14S log(4AT/δ)/n).
Let (a_n)_(n≥1) be real with |a_n|≤Kn for a finite K, and suppose |a_(m+n)−a_m−a_n|≤C for a finite C≥0 and all positive integers m,n. Then a_n/n has a finite limit.

published_dependencies.used_for: The measurable space S×[0,1] and reward-coordinate measurability.
Each admissible pair's joint next-state/reward probability law.
Pointwise probability sections and measurable event sections of the MDP kernel.
Mean rewards, possibly infinite hitting-time expectations, finite-horizon values and expected regret.
Policy path laws and the independent finite sample-tape construction under Choice.
Explicit inherited assumptions for path laws, conditional expectations and Pinsker.
Infinite hitting times and the extended order used for diameter.
Extended infima of policy hitting-time expectations.
Centered tape coordinates in the confidence-bound proof.
Converting centered tape-coordinate sums into martingales before applying Azuma.
Width-one reward/subset concentration and predictable-width transition and reward martingale bounds in realized regret.
Conditional continuation inequalities in finite-horizon dynamic programming and common-gain existence.
Passing conditional continuation bounds to unconditional finite-horizon reward bounds.
Finite reward-sum identities, expected-regret linearity and expectation inequalities.
Natural-log relative entropy and its direction in the finite-history likelihood-ratio calculation.
Bounding event-supremum total variation by sqrt(KL(P₀‖P_j)/2) in the lower-bound testing argument.
The nonnegative [0,T] version bounds visit-count expectation differences by T times total variation.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier definition against both consuming definitions. The supplier permits empty state sets and has a finite reward alphabet; the consumers explicitly restrict to nonempty states and locally define the Borel [0,1] joint-kernel extension. They use the supplier's finite state/action skeleton without attributing the extended reward model or history-dependent policy interface to it.
